findings.description: The 'data' bucket is created with no ACL restriction, no public access block, and no bucket policy restricting access — the comments explicitly note the bucket is public. Any object stored in it, including sensitive customer data, may be readable by anyone on the internet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including customer-master.xlsx) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this public bucket would leave no S3 server access log trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is disabled, so objects deleted or overwritten by an attacker (combined with force_destroy = true) cannot be recovered, aiding destructive or ransomware attacks.

A customer master data spreadsheet is uploaded into the unencrypted, publicly accessible 'data' bucket and is itself defined without server-side encryption (kms_key_id), exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket holding financial data, removing the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so financial objects can be irreversibly deleted or overwritten with no recovery path.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a future ACL or bucket policy change could make private financial data public without any account-level guardrail.
The operations bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so there is no server access log record of reads and writes for this bucket.
No public access block resource restricts this bucket, so a subsequent ACL or policy change could expose it publicly without an account guardrail.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, leaving the bucket without a guardrail against future public ACLs or policies.
The central log bucket has no public access block; because it aggregates access logs from other buckets, accidental exposure would leak activity metadata about the environment.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows Terraform to delete all stored access logs, and there is no MFA delete or object lock, weakening the integrity of the audit trail.
